sourcedFrom: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL Q5 MATCH SF PISTOLS — rev a — carried in the publisher's own file designation 2846993 rev a (UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages)
cleanIntro: Walther Arms publishes a book for this pistol by name: 'Q5 Match SF Pistols'. It is not a polymer PPQ with a heavier frame - the strip is different. The Q5 Match SF comes apart with a rotating take down lever, turned up while the slide is locked open, and the trigger has to be pressed on an empty gun before the slide will come forward off the frame.

steps.title: Know your magazine release - a push button that may have been reversed
steps.action: Find the magazine release before you start: it is the thumb-operated push button on the side of the grip, behind the trigger guard. Walther makes it reversible, so on a left-handed owner's pistol it may be on the right side.
steps.prose: This is the control you use in the very next step, and on a second-hand pistol it is worth a look rather than an assumption. The slide release is ambidextrous; the magazine button is not - it lives on one side only, whichever side it was last set to.
steps.quote: The slide release is ambidextrous and the thumb operated magazine release push button, conveniently located on the frame, is reversible for either left- or right-hand use.
steps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL Q5 MATCH SF PISTOLS — rev a — carried in the publisher's own file designation 2846993 rev a — 3.1 Main Features, printed p.11 (PDF p.11)

steps.title: Magazine out first
steps.action: Point the pistol in a safe direction with your finger off the trigger and out of the trigger guard. Depress the magazine release and remove the magazine.
steps.prose: Magazine before slide, every time. The Q5 Match SF has no magazine disconnect, so taking the magazine out does nothing to make the pistol safe on its own - it only stops the next rack from feeding a fresh round.
steps.quote: Depress the magazine release and remove the magazine (5.1.1 Fig. 1).
steps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL Q5 MATCH SF PISTOLS — rev a — carried in the publisher's own file designation 2846993 rev a — 5.1.1 Field-Stripping Disassembly, printed p.23 (PDF p.23)
steps.warn: THE Q5 MATCH SF IS NOT EQUIPPED WITH A MAGAZINE DISCONNECT FEATURE.

steps.title: Rack briskly to throw out any chambered round
steps.action: Muzzle safe, finger still off the trigger, grasp the serrated sides of the slide from the rear with thumb and fingers and briskly draw the slide fully rearward to extract any cartridge from the chamber and clear it from the pistol.
steps.prose: Briskly is the word that matters. A slow, gentle rack can leave a round balanced in the port instead of throwing it clear. Hold the rear serrations so your hand is not over the ejection port.
steps.quote: and briskly draw the slide fully rearward in order to extract any cartridge from the barrel chamber and clear it from the pistol.
steps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL Q5 MATCH SF PISTOLS — rev a — carried in the publisher's own file designation 2846993 rev a — 5.1.1 Field-Stripping Disassembly, printed p.23 (PDF p.23)

steps.title: Lock it open, then look into the chamber AND down the magazine well
steps.action: Pull the slide fully to the rear and press upward on the slide stop lever while letting the slide move slightly forward, so it locks open. Look into the chamber and down through the magazine well and verify that no ammunition remains in the pistol.
steps.prose: Two openings, two looks, and the slide stays locked open for the next step anyway - the take down lever is turned with the slide back. Do not use the red loaded chamber indicator on the extractor as your check; Walther warns against exactly that, because solvent, wear or dirt can hide the red.
steps.quote: Look into the chamber and down through the magazine well. Verify that no ammunition remains in the pistol
steps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL Q5 MATCH SF PISTOLS — rev a — carried in the publisher's own file designation 2846993 rev a — 5.1.1 Field-Stripping Disassembly, printed p.24 (PDF p.24)
steps.warn: DO NOT RELY UPON THE LOADED CHAMBER INDICATOR TO VERIFY THE PRESENCE OR ABSENCE OF A ROUND IN THE CHAMBER.

steps.title: With the slide locked open, turn the take down lever up
steps.action: With the slide still locked open, rotate the take down lever clockwise upwards until it stops.
steps.prose: This is where the Q5 Match SF parts company with the polymer PPQ: there is no two-sided catch to pull down, just one lever on the left of the frame that swings up. Do it while the slide is locked back - that is the order the book gives - and turn it to its stop, not part way.
steps.quote: Rotate the take down lever clockwise upwards until it stops.
steps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL Q5 MATCH SF PISTOLS — rev a — carried in the publisher's own file designation 2846993 rev a — 5.1.1 Field-Stripping Disassembly, printed p.24 (PDF p.24)

steps.title: Close the slide gently
steps.action: Pull the slide slightly to the rear to free it from the slide stop, then slowly release it and let it return to the forward position.
steps.prose: Ride it forward rather than letting it slam. The gun is empty - you have looked twice - and there is no reason to put the slide into battery hard against a lever you have just moved.
steps.quote: Close the slide: Pull the slide slightly to the rear.
steps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL Q5 MATCH SF PISTOLS — rev a — carried in the publisher's own file designation 2846993 rev a — 5.1.1 Field-Stripping Disassembly, printed p.24 (PDF p.24)

steps.title: Press the trigger - the step every check above exists for
steps.action: Point the pistol in a safe direction and squeeze the trigger fully to the rear. Then take your finger off the trigger and out of the trigger guard.
steps.prose: The striker has to be released before the slide will come forward off the frame, so this press is not optional. Walther puts a full warning here: if a live round were left in the chamber the pistol would fire. If you skipped either look a moment ago, go back now rather than pressing on trust.
steps.quote: Point the pistol in a safe direction. Squeeze the trigger fully to the rear.
steps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL Q5 MATCH SF PISTOLS — rev a — carried in the publisher's own file designation 2846993 rev a — 5.1.1 Field-Stripping Disassembly, printed p.24 (PDF p.24)
steps.warn: TO COMPLETE DISASSEMBLY, YOU WILL BE REQUIRED TO PULL THE TRIGGER.

steps.title: Slide forward and off the frame
steps.action: Move the slide forward and remove it from the frame.
steps.prose: It runs forward off the rails with the barrel and recoil spring still inside it. If it will not move, the striker has not been released or the take down lever is not fully up - check the lever before forcing anything.
steps.quote: Move the slide forward, and remove it from the frame.
steps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL Q5 MATCH SF PISTOLS — rev a — carried in the publisher's own file designation 2846993 rev a — 5.1.1 Field-Stripping Disassembly, printed p.24 (PDF p.24)

steps.title: Recoil guide rod assembly out from under the barrel
steps.action: Remove the recoil guide rod assembly from below the barrel while compressing the spring.
steps.prose: Compress it a little first so the large end comes off the barrel recess instead of being pried out of it. The assembly is held together by a locking ring and stays in one piece; the spring is strong, so keep a grip on it.
steps.quote: Remove the recoil guide rod assembly from below the barrel while compressing the spring (5.1.1 Fig. 6).
steps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL Q5 MATCH SF PISTOLS — rev a — carried in the publisher's own file designation 2846993 rev a — 5.1.1 Field-Stripping Disassembly, printed p.24 (PDF p.24)

steps.title: Thread protector if fitted, then the barrel out of the slide
steps.action: If your barrel is threaded, remove the thread protector by turning it counter clockwise. Then remove the barrel from the slide.
steps.prose: Only a threaded barrel has a protector; a plain muzzle has nothing to unscrew. The barrel then lifts out of the slide - note how its locking lugs sit, because it goes back in the same way.
steps.quote: Remove the thread protector by turning it counter clockwise. (If barrel is threaded)
steps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL Q5 MATCH SF PISTOLS — rev a — carried in the publisher's own file designation 2846993 rev a — 5.1.1 Field-Stripping Disassembly, printed p.25 (PDF p.25)

steps.title: Field strip complete - frame, slide, barrel, recoil guide rod, magazine
steps.action: That is the full field strip. Walther tells you never to go further than the procedures its own book publishes - for this pistol, the striker, the extractor and the magazine.
steps.prose: Everything routine is reachable now: the bore from the chamber end, the breech face, the extractor claw, the barrel's locking surfaces and cam ramp, and the frame rails. The deep clean below needs a 5/64-inch (2 mm) drift punch and a 5/32-inch (4 mm) punch.
steps.quote: Remove the barrel from the slide.
steps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL Q5 MATCH SF PISTOLS — rev a — carried in the publisher's own file designation 2846993 rev a — 5.1.1 Field-Stripping Disassembly, printed p.25 (PDF p.25)
steps.warn: NEVER DISASSEMBLE YOUR HANDGUN BEYOND THE FIELD STRIPPING PROCESS OUTLINED IN THIS MANUAL.

deepSteps.title: Slide end cap off with a 5/64-inch punch
deepSteps.action: With the pistol field stripped, stand the slide muzzle-down on a smooth flat surface, grasp the rear serrations, push in the pin through the square opening at the top right of the slide end cap with a 5/64" (2 mm) drift punch, and slide the end cap downwards off the slide.
deepSteps.prose: The end cap is holding the striker spring, so one hand keeps the slide pressed down on the bench while the other works the punch. The pin is pushed in, not driven out - it only has to move far enough to free the cap.
deepSteps.quote: Place the muzzle end of the slide on a smooth, flat surface.
deepSteps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL Q5 MATCH SF PISTOLS — rev a — carried in the publisher's own file designation 2846993 rev a — 5.2.1 Remove Striker Assembly, printed p.26 (PDF p.26)
deepSteps.warn: WEAR SAFETY GLASSES EVERY TIME YOU ASSEMBLE OR DISASSEMBLE YOUR FIREARM.

deepSteps.title: Striker assembly out of the slide
deepSteps.action: Remove the striker assembly from the slide.
deepSteps.prose: It comes out rearward as one captive unit. Leave it whole - the book publishes no procedure inside it - and keep it clean and dry.
deepSteps.quote: Remove the striker assembly from the slide (5.2.1 Fig. 3).
deepSteps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL Q5 MATCH SF PISTOLS — rev a — carried in the publisher's own file designation 2846993 rev a — 5.2.1 Remove Striker Assembly, printed p.26 (PDF p.26)

deepSteps.title: The striker channel stays DRY
deepSteps.action: Clean the striker channel and the striker assembly dry. Do not put lubricant inside the striker assembly.
deepSteps.prose: Oil in the channel gathers powder and carbon into a paste that slows the striker, and a slow striker gives light primer strikes. Walther says the channel is designed to let the striker move freely without lubricant.
deepSteps.quote: Do not lubricate inside the striker assembly, this creates the potential for residue build up
deepSteps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL Q5 MATCH SF PISTOLS — rev a — carried in the publisher's own file designation 2846993 rev a — 5.7 Lubrication, caution, printed p.32 (PDF p.32)

deepSteps.title: Extractor out - only with the striker already removed
deepSteps.action: With the striker out, place the slide upside down with the muzzle to the left. Use the 5/64" (2 mm) drift punch to force the extractor pin into the slide against its spring until the rear of the extractor pops out, then remove the punch.
deepSteps.prose: Walther's note is that the striker interferes with the striker safety, which is why this comes after the striker. Only do it when you have a reason - grit behind the claw or an extraction problem - because two small sprung parts are about to be loose.
deepSteps.quote: Use a 5/64” (2 mm) drift punch to force the extractor pin into the slide against the spring force (5.3.1 Fig. 1) until the rear end of the extractor pops out.
deepSteps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL Q5 MATCH SF PISTOLS — rev a — carried in the publisher's own file designation 2846993 rev a — 5.3.1 Remove Extractor, printed p.27 (PDF p.27)
deepSteps.warn: WEAR SAFETY GLASSES, AND WHILE YOU REMOVE THE EXTRACTOR, BE SURE TO CONTROL THE STRIKER SAFETY

deepSteps.title: Finger over the plungers as the extractor pivots out
deepSteps.action: Keep a finger over the striker safety and the extractor plunger while you pivot the extractor out, then remove the striker safety assembly and the extractor plunger assembly from the slide. Leave the extractor spring in its seat inside the extractor slot.
deepSteps.prose: Both plungers are sprung and both will leave the slide fast if uncovered. The extractor spring is the stopping point: it has a larger end coil that keeps it in its slot, and the book tells you not to take it out.
deepSteps.quote: Do not remove the extractor spring from its seat inside the extractor slot.
deepSteps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL Q5 MATCH SF PISTOLS — rev a — carried in the publisher's own file designation 2846993 rev a — 5.3.1 Remove Extractor, printed p.27 (PDF p.27)

deepSteps.title: Magazine floorplate off with a 5/32-inch punch
deepSteps.action: Using a 5/32" (4 mm) punch, depress the floorplate catch through the hole in the floorplate, slide the floorplate forward off the tube while keeping the catch pressed, then remove the catch and spring through the bottom and turn the tube right side up to remove the follower.
deepSteps.prose: The spring is compressed the length of the tube and the catch is all that holds it, so keep a thumb over the bottom as the floorplate slides. An extended magazine has a metal tab at the rear base that is pushed up with a flat screwdriver first.
deepSteps.quote: Using a 5/32” (4 mm) punch, depress the floorplate catch through the hole in the floorplate (5.4.1 Fig. 1).
deepSteps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL Q5 MATCH SF PISTOLS — rev a — carried in the publisher's own file designation 2846993 rev a — 5.4.1 Magazine Disassembly, printed p.28 (PDF p.28)
deepSteps.warn: THE MAGAZINE SPRING IS UNDER PRESSURE. USE CAUTION WHEN STRIPPING DOWN THE MAGAZINE.

deepSteps.title: Only PPQ M-Series magazines - never P99 or PPQ Classic
deepSteps.action: Keep to the magazines Walther specifies for this pistol: PPQ M-Series magazines. P99 and PPQ Classic magazines will not work in it.
deepSteps.prose: They may look close enough to fit, and that is the trap. Keep this pistol's magazines marked and together, and do not let a P99 or Classic magazine into its box.
deepSteps.quote: P99 magazines and PPQ Classic magazines will not work in Q5 Match SF pistols.
deepSteps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL Q5 MATCH SF PISTOLS — rev a — carried in the publisher's own file designation 2846993 rev a — 5.4 Magazine, caution, printed p.28 (PDF p.28)

deepSteps.title: Deep clean complete - the recoil guide rod stays assembled
deepSteps.action: Do not take the recoil guide rod assembly apart for cleaning. Walther says it is not necessary for maintenance and should be avoided; the spring is under enormous tension.
deepSteps.prose: The book does print a procedure for it, with a 10 mm wrench and a C-shaped locking ring, but it frames that as something to avoid when maintaining the pistol. Wipe the rod and spring down whole. Anything past the striker, extractor and magazine is a gunsmith's job with genuine Walther parts.
deepSteps.quote: It is not necessary to dismantle the recoil guide rod assembly when maintaining the pistol, and this should be avoided.
deepSteps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL Q5 MATCH SF PISTOLS — rev a — carried in the publisher's own file designation 2846993 rev a — 5.5 Recoil guide rod assembly, printed p.29 (PDF p.29)

cleaning.name: BARREL & BREECH
tasks: From the chamber end, push a brush through the bore until the bristles fully exit at the muzzle, then pull it back until they fully exit at the chamber end
Use a powder-removing solvent and a brass bristle bore brush to take lead and firing residue out of the barrel, then wipe with patches
With a small brush dipped in solvent, clear deposits from the breech face, the chamber end of the barrel, the extractor and the areas around them
Clean the ramp where the locking block cams the barrel

cleaning.name: SLIDE, FRAME & STRIKER CHANNEL
tasks: Remove residue on the steel frame with light brushing and a solvent
Wipe the slide guides and the frame rails before any oil goes on them
Keep the striker channel DRY - no oil in it at all
Avoid prolonged solvent immersion and prolonged ultrasonic cleaning (no hotter than 122 °F / 50 °C)
Do not use ammonia-based or other strong alkaline solvents on a Walther

cleaning.name: LUBRICATION & MAGAZINE
tasks: A light film of high quality gun lubricant on all external metal surfaces, then wipe clean - never so much that it drips
Barrel: a light film on the outside and on the cam ramp
One drop on the slide guides and one on the trigger bar
One drop on the safety plunger and one in the disconnector cut of the slide
A light film on the magazine's external metal surfaces
In a cold climate, use a lubricant that will not congeal at low temperatures

reassembly: Hold the slide upside down and place the barrel inside it with the locking lugs oriented as the book shows.
Refit the thread protector if your barrel is threaded.
Insert the recoil guide rod assembly: small end of the rod into the spring mounting at the front of the slide, large end into the lower barrel recess, compressing the spring.
Push the slide from the front onto the slide guides of the frame.
Pull the slide fully rearward and press up on the slide stop lever to lock it open.
Rotate the take down lever counter-clockwise downwards until it stops.
Pull the slide fully to the rear and guide it forward to its closed position.
fncheck: With the magazine out and the chamber confirmed empty: the take down lever should sit fully down against its stop; the slide should run its full stroke and return to battery under spring pressure; it should lock open on the slide stop and release cleanly when you press the stop down; the trigger should have its consistent pull and a reset you can feel; and the push-button magazine release should drop an empty magazine free. With the slide locked open, look at the breech face: if the striker is protruding, Walther says do not use the pistol and take it to an authorized Walther gunsmith.
